name: labcmp-impl
description: the IMPLEMENTATION half of the side-by-side, on the same fixture and the same gesture as labcmp-lab. The page it shows is a plain fixture rather than the lab, so the capture holds Atrium's own sidebar and nothing else. Captures only; the comparison is a person reading the paired frames, because a pixel diff between two surfaces that were never pixel-identical would be noise. Also captures the Overview through cmd+shift+o, so the two Overviews can be read against each other.

actions.note: the same wait its partner takes, so neither side is caught mid-load
the implementation at rest: sidebar, tab rows, dots bar
toggleOverview, the binding the hotkeys store carries
the Overview builds its sections on open
Atrium's Overview, to read against the lab's own

assertions.desc: sanity: the browser window alone. This read 2 while Overview was a separate widget over the page. That widget is retired and the rail's leading pane is the only Overview, the way the lab has it, so a second window here would mean the widget is back.

assertions.label: the-page-stays-visible-beside-overview
assertions.desc: The whole point of the task: the user reported three times that opening Overview covered the page. The page here is white, so anything drawn over it pulls the mean down. ax_window_count above catches Overview returning as a second WINDOW - this catches it returning as an overlay inside one. Measured 254.0 with Overview open, against 222.5 under the retired widget.
assertions.note: Not 300,600,400,60, which would read the foot of the Overview WINDOW. That window is gone, so the old region lands on the page and can only read white.

assertions.label: overview-really-opened-in-the-sidebar
assertions.desc: The presence half, without which the check above passes just as well when Overview never opens at all. This is the foot of the widened sidebar: measured 122.7 with the Overview pane parked there and 185.6 at rest, so the band excludes rest. The floor of 5 stops a black frame - a capture that never rendered - from passing.
